name: Eva Moss
life: “I still remember bringing groceries to a colleague without asking about the case.” People around the corner by Juniper Tailor know Eva by a small Thursday habit. Eva looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I visited the family off duty. I am learning which parts of that visit never belong in the break room.
appearance: Eva has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a gray fisher's sweater. It usually goes with a little coil of soft measuring tape. When somebody else has the floor, Eva grins on one side while the eyes stay serious.
personality: Eva talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Eva's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To keep family visits separate from workplace accounts.
family: Eli Mason is Eva’s half-sibling. Eva brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Eli makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The painted footprint*, Eli says, “I drew it with house paint because the lifeguard had used up all our chalk.”
connections: Leo Hart. Private family information only reaches the station with the returning worker's say.

reactions.situation: The returning colleague finds another name on the desk
reactions.response: Eva lets both workers describe what happened to the assignment during leave.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Eva asks the neighbor privately what they want, without treating their place as something for sale.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Eva says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
